note: Both sets capture the same core facts from the page: 50-degree solar altitude at fall equinox 12pm, 0 window azimuth for the southern exposed louver, the Height = Depth*tan(solar elevation)/Cos(solar azimuth – window azimuth) algorithm, the 1:1 depth-to-height ratio, the truncated isosceles triangle louver shape, and the 25-degree structural bend. Set A duplicates the shape claim and adds two solar-altitude claims, one of which misbinds the site-specific solar altitude to the Harvest Shade Screen and one with a vague entity ('solar altitude | value'). Set B duplicates the shape claim and repeats the 25-degree bend claim three times, with one instance misreading 'longitudinal' as 'longitude' and one vague 'solar altitude | value' claim. Each set therefore has roughly one misread/misbound claim and one vague claim on top of shared duplicates, so they are effectively equivalent.
